name: correlation_regime_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: Individual stocks' correlation with their parent index (NIFTY 50 or Bank NIFTY) varies intraday. When a stock's rolling 30-bar correlation with the index drops below 0.3 (decoupled), the stock is driven by idiosyncratic factors — if these are positive (stock up, index flat), the move tends to persist (information-driven). When correlation is high (> 0.7), the stock moves mechanically with the index — better to trade the index directly. We trade only in the decoupled regime, buying stocks that are up while the index is flat (positive alpha) and shorting stocks that are down while the index is flat (negative alpha). The inefficiency exists because most traders don't compute real-time stock-index correlation.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > ₹100 Cr; historical beta to NIFTY between 0.7 and 1.5

indicators.name: Alpha_30
indicators.params: sum(Stock_Returns, 30) - beta * sum(NIFTY_Returns, 30) where beta = historical_beta_60d

conditions: Alpha_30 > 20 bps (stock generating positive alpha while decoupled)
NIFTY_Flat == True (index is flat — confirming idiosyncratic move)
long.confirmation: Alpha_30 has been positive for at least 10 bars (not a transient spike)

conditions: Alpha_30 < -20 bps (stock generating negative alpha while decoupled)
short.confirmation: Alpha_30 has been negative for at least 10 bars

exit.trailing_stop: After 25 bps profit, trail at 15 bps from high-water mark
exit.signal_exit: Rolling_Corr_30 rises above 0.50 (stock re-coupling with index — idiosyncratic edge gone)

risk.position_sizing: Fixed ₹1L; increase to ₹1.25L if abs(Alpha_30) > 40 bps (strong alpha signal)

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 22 (high VIX = high correlation = fewer decoupled opportunities)
filters.time_filter: No entries before 09:45 (need 30 bars for correlation) or after 15:10
filters.volume_filter: Stock volume > SMA(volume, 20) during decoupled period
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY_Flat must be True (abs NIFTY 30-bar return < 15 bps)
filters.event_filter: Skip if stock has corporate action or earnings — decoupling may be event-driven and ephemeral
other_filters: Historical beta must be between 0.7-1.5 for meaningful correlation measurement

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — real-time correlation monitoring is computationally non-trivial; the concept of trading alpha during decoupled periods is less explored in retail

weaknesses: Correlation computed on 30 1-min returns has very wide confidence intervals — at 30 observations, a measured correlation of 0.30 has a 95% CI of roughly [0.0, 0.55], making the threshold unreliable

NIFTY_Flat requirement (abs return < 15 bps over 30 bars) is very restrictive — during active market hours, NIFTY rarely stays within 15 bps for 30 minutes, limiting opportunities to low-volume periods
Decoupling often occurs during news/events specific to the stock — these are precisely the situations where the stock may gap further in either direction, making the 25 bps stop inadequate
prior_art: Pairs trading (Gatev et al. 2006) uses correlation; stock-index relative value strategies at hedge funds; correlation breakdown discussed in Cont & Wagalath (2013); intraday alpha decomposition less documented
notes: Consider relaxing NIFTY_Flat to abs return < 30 bps for more frequent signals. The beta used for alpha computation should be re-estimated weekly to capture evolving stock-index relationship.
